name: Mariner 4
payload: Mars flyby spacecraft with TV camera (Mariner C, 260.8 kg)
significance: Mariner 4 took the first close-up pictures of another planet. Its 21 grainy images of Mars, returned in July 1965, showed a cratered, Moon-like surface instead of the canals and vegetation people had long imagined. As it passed behind the planet, its radio signal revealed an atmosphere far thinner than expected, about 1% of Earth's, and it found no magnetic field. Together these results ended the idea of Mars as a living, Earth-like world and set the agenda for every Mars mission since.
statusNote: Launched 1964-11-28 14:22:01 UT on an Atlas-Agena D from Cape Kennedy, with a new all-metal shroud. One mid-course correction on 1964-12-05. Closest approach 9,846 km at 01:00:57 UT on 1965-07-15; 21 images plus part of a 22nd were taken, and a radio occultation measured a surface pressure of about 4-7 mb. Contact until 1965-10-01 at 309 million km; reactivated in 1967 for engineering tests; final contact 1967-12-21 per NSSDCA, 1967-12-31 per Siddiqi (Siddiqi, Beyond Earth; NASA NSSDCA). Path calculated: a two-body transfer between the real launch and arrival dates; no measured trajectory exists, so it is drawn dashed. For comparison, arcs drawn this way for modern direct flights fall within ~0.002 AU of their real JPL Horizons trajectories.
